name: Troccas
description: Troccas is a traditional Swiss Tarot game played in the Romansh-speaking Surselva region of Grisons. It uses a 78-card Swiss 1JJ Tarot deck with Italian suits. Notable for the 'King and Jack Rule' (King demands Jack surrender) and coded signals (Tschintschar). Partnership play for 4.

overview.description: Troccas is a traditional Swiss Tarot game played in the Romansh-speaking Surselva region of Grisons. It uses a 78-card Swiss 1JJ Tarot deck with Italian suits. Notable for the 'King and Jack Rule' (King demands Jack surrender) and coded signals (Tschintschar). Partnership play for 4.

history.origins: Although the exact history is uncertain, Troccas is thought to have been imported from Italy to Switzerland in the seventeenth century. It took root in the Romansh-speaking Canton Grisons, especially the Surselva region from the Medel and Tujetsch valleys to Ilanz, and has been preserved there as a living tradition. In recent decades it has gained in popularity, with local clubs and tournaments; scholarly accounts include Carla Deplazes' work on Graubünden tarot and tournament rules from Savognin.
timeline: 17th century: Game arrived in Switzerland from Italy.
history.cultural: Recognized as living tradition of Switzerland.

setup.deck: 78 cards: 4 suits x 14 + 21 trumps + Fool. Points: K/Bagat/TrXXI/Fool=5, Q=4, Cav=3, J=2, others=1. Count in groups of 4, subtract 3. Total 72.
setup.dealing: 19 each (dealer gets 21, discards 2). Last card face up.

rules.objective: Score more card points than opponent team (target 36 to break even).
rules.gameplay: Follow suit. Must trump if void. Fool excuses from following. King and Jack Rule: When King is first played in a suit, winner demands the Jack of that suit. Counterclockwise play.

strategy.basic: Play Kings early to trigger Jack Rule. Protect Honors (1, 21, Fool).
strategy.advanced: Manage trump count. Force opponent Honors out.
